verdict.summary: Strava's published API Policy prohibits using Strava API materials or data in an AI application. The prohibition includes agent workflows, context-window ingestion, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation. Ordinary OAuth scopes and app-capacity review do not provide a published exception. Do not build or submit this AI integration through the ordinary Developer Application flow.
verdict.activeEffort: 4–10 days (sum of the step estimates below). Not applicable: the published policy prohibits this AI use.
verdict.waitTime: Not applicable: no published permission or app-review path authorizes this AI use.
verdict.mainGate: The published AI policy prohibits this use. Ordinary app review does not remove that prohibition.

steps.title: Obtain written AI permission

detail.text: Strava's published policy prohibits using Strava API Materials or Strava Data in connection with an AI Application. Do not treat a written-permission request as a documented approval path. Do not build or submit this AI integration through the ordinary Developer Application flow.

sources.quote: You may not use the Strava API Materials or Strava Data, directly or indirectly, in connection with the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI Application.

steps.output: Written approval for the exact data flow and AI use.

steps.title: Create the developer app

detail.text: A Strava subscription is required to create a Developer Application. Creating a normal app does not authorize an AI application. Use this setup flow only for a non-AI application that complies with Strava's policy.

sources.quote: A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app.
After you are logged in, go to https://www.strava.com/settings/api and create an app.

detail.text: In API Settings, set Authorization Callback Domain to your production domain. Use localhost only during local development.

steps.title: Test with your account

detail.text: Single Player Mode allows testing only with your own Strava account. The published AI prohibition still applies, so do not use this mode to test an AI integration that uses Strava API materials or data.

steps.title: Submit the review form

detail.text: For a non-AI application, submit the Developer Program form when you need more than 10 connected customers. Include every Strava data screen and every Connect with Strava button. This capacity review is not a published exception to the AI prohibition.

sources.quote: If you want to scale beyond 10 connected athletes you’ll need to submit your app for review.
Please complete our Developer Program form for review and be sure to include screenshots of all the places Strava data is shown and the ‘Connect with Strava’ button in your application.

steps.title: Wait for review

detail.text: For a non-AI application's capacity request, wait for Strava's review after submission. The reported 7–10-business-day time is a target, not a service commitment. Capacity approval does not authorize an AI use prohibited by the policy.

sources.quote: The review process typically takes between 7-10 business days, unless we require any additional information regarding your app.
